title: A2-07 · ‎كَانَand the verbs of his family

blocks.text: A2-07 · ⁧كَانَ⁩ and the verbs of his family
Lesson overview

With ⁧كَانَ⁩ you said "it was" and "it was" (A1-18). In this unit ⁧كَانَ⁩ It becomes an instrument of the story: with the imperfect form the usual past (I lived, I worked, every summer we went...) that in Arabic does not have a proper time. Learn also verbs that work as ⁧كَانَ⁩ and they are used to talk about changes: ⁧صَارَ⁩ and ⁧أَصْبَحَ⁩ "become', ⁧مَا زَالَ⁩ and ⁧لَا يَزَالُ⁩ continue to do so. And learn to describe a person: colors, hair, glasses, beard. A week.

rows: A2 · Module A2.2 The name and the phrase
6–7 hours · one week (week 61 of the calendar)

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-07), script for speech synthesis, session with tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. use ⁧كَانَ⁩ in all the times and ways studied, with the predicate to the accusative;
2. narrating past habits and situations with ⁧كَانَ⁩ + imperfect, distinguishing them from punctual actions to perfect;
3. talk about changes with ⁧صَارَ⁩ and ⁧أَصْبَحَ⁩ , and what goes on with ⁧مَا زَالَ⁩ and ⁧لَا يَزَالُ⁩ ;
4. describe the appearance of a person: height, body shape, hair, colors, special signs;
5. read a vocalized text without endings, as you read aloud a modern text.

blocks.text: What to notice. ⁧كُنْتُ طَالِبَةً⁩ I was a student. ⁧كَانَ⁩ The predicate is accusative. ⁧كُنْتُ أَسْكُنُ⁩ , ⁧كُنْتُ أَدْرُسُ⁩ I lived, I studied, ⁧كَانَ⁩ + imperfect is the usual past. ⁧تَعَرَّفْتُ عَلَى⁩ I met (one person) and ⁧تَغَيَّرَ⁩ It's changed, it's punctual: perfect. ⁧أَصْبَحَتْ⁩ , ⁧صَارَتْ⁩ It has become de facto with the predicate to the accusative ( ⁧مَدِينَتَكِ⁩ ). ⁧مَا زِلْتُ أَشْتَاقُ⁩ I still miss it. ⁧مَا زَالَ⁩ + imperfect. ⁧عِنْدَمَا⁩ When (A2-14). ⁧لَمْ تَكُنْ هُنَاكَ مَطَاعِمُ⁩ : the verb is female because the subject ⁧مَطَاعِم⁩ It's a plural of things.
2. ⁧كَانَ⁩ at all times; ⁧كَانَ⁩ + imperfect
The forms of ⁧كَانَ⁩ . It is a concave verb (A2-02, A2-03, A2-05): now you know all its forms.

With all these forms the nominal predicate is to the accusative: ⁧كَانَ الطَّرِيقُ مُزْدَحِمًا⁩ , ⁧سَيَكُونُ الجَوُّ جَمِيلًا⁩ , ⁧لَنْ أَكُونَ مَشْغُولًا⁩ . The subject remains on the name. The imperfect One ⁧يَكُونُ⁩ in the present it is used for usual or general situations (....)..........) because the simple nominal phrase has no verb. ⁧كَانَ⁩ + imperfect: the usual and ongoing past. Arabic has only one past time, the perfect one, expressing the finished action (I studied, I studied). For the usual or ongoing action in the past it is used ⁧كَانَ⁩ to the perfect + verb to the imperfect, both to the same person.

rows: As a boy, I studied every night.
When you called, I was studying.

blocks.text: Agreement. When the subject is expressed after ⁧كَانَ⁩ , ⁧كَانَ⁩ remains singular (rule of the verb before the subject) but the second verb agrees: ⁧كَانَ الطُّلَّابُ يَدْرُسُونَ⁩ The students were studying. With the subject first, both agree: ⁧الطُّلَّابُ كَانُوا يَدْرُسُونَ⁩ . Denial. It's usually denied. ⁧كَانَ⁩ : ⁧لَمْ يَكُنْ يَعْرِفُ⁩ "He did not know" ⁧مَا كُنْتُ أَفْهَمُ⁩ I didn't understand. It is also possible ⁧كَانَ لَا يَعْرِفُ⁩ , with the same meaning. ⁧كَانَ يَجِبُ أَنْ⁩ ... I would have / should have... ⁧كَانَ يَجِبُ أَنْ تَتَّصِلَ بِي⁩ You should have called me. ⁧يَجِبُ⁩ remains unchanged (A2-04).
3. Become: ⁧صَارَ⁩ and ⁧أَصْبَحَ⁩

How ⁧كَانَ⁩ , they want to preach to the accused. They are almost synonymous; ⁧أَصْبَحَ⁩ is a little more formal and is the most frequent in written texts. The future and denial are regular: ⁧سَيُصْبِحُ⁩ , ⁧لَمْ يُصْبِحْ⁩ , ⁧لَمْ يَصِرْ⁩ . With the imperfect, ⁧صَارَ⁩ / ⁧أَصْبَحَ⁩ indicate that an action has become habitual or has begun: ⁧أَصْبَحَ يَعْمَلُ فِي رُومَا⁩ He is now working in Rome, he has started working in Rome. ⁧صِرْتُ أَفْهَمُ الأَخْبَارَ⁩ I understand the news now.
4. More, continue to do so: ⁧مَا زَالَ⁩ and ⁧لَا يَزَالُ⁩

⁧مَا زَالَ⁩ (perfect denied) and ⁧لَا يَزَالُ⁩ (Imperfect denied) literally mean "not ceased," i.e. "yet, continue to" . They're built like ⁧كَانَ⁩ : with a predicate to the accusative or with a verb to the imperfect.
They (m.) ⁧لَا يَزَالُونَمَا زَالُوا⁩
• ⁧مَا زَالَ الوَضْعُ صَعْبًا.⁩ The situation is still difficult.
• ⁧لَا تَزَالُ تَسْكُنُ فِي بَيْرُوتَ.⁩ She still lives in Beirut.
• ⁧مَا زِلْتُ لَا أَفْهَمُ.⁩ I still don't understand.

The two verbs have the same meaning; ⁧لَا يَزَالُ⁩ is more frequent in the journalistic language. The opposite is ⁧لَمْ يَعُدْ⁩ Not... more...A2-05): ⁧مَا زَالَ يَعْمَلُ هُنَا⁩ It still works here. ⁧لَمْ يَعُدْ يَعْمَلُ هُنَا⁩ It doesn't work here anymore. To be recognised: ⁧ظَلَّ⁩ • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • ⁧ظَلَّ وَاقِفًا⁩ It remained in its standing, ⁧ظَلَّ يَنْتَظِرُ سَاعَةً⁩ It continued to wait for one hour. All these verbs, with ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ , form the family of ⁧كَانَ⁩ » ( ⁧كَانَ وَأَخَوَاتُهَا⁩ ), that Arab grammars deal together precisely because they place the predicate to the accusative.

6. Reading a text without termination

Up to now the course texts have been vocized in full, including the final vowels of the cases. In reality, almost no one reads a modern text with all the endings: they read the words with their internal vowels and let the final vowel fall, as in the reading on pause. Reading 1 of this unit is written as follows: internal vowels yes, endings no. What falls: the final vowels of the cases and the tanwīn names and adjectives ( ⁧المَدِينَة⁩ , ⁧شَقَّة صَغِيرَة⁩ ), and the final -u of the imperfect ( ⁧يَعْمَل⁩ , ⁧نَلْعَب⁩ ). What remains written:
• the tanwīn -an ( ⁧بَارِدا⁩ , ⁧مُزْدَحِما⁩ ), which reads -a pause or -an if you want;
• the personal suffixes of the verbs and the -a of the perfect ( ⁧كَانُوا⁩ , ⁧يَسْكُنُونَ⁩ , ⁧كَانَتْ⁩ , ⁧كَانَ⁩ ): are not case-law;
• vowels that are part of the word ( ⁧هُنَاكَ⁩ , ⁧الآنَ⁩ , ⁧ذٰلِكَ⁩ , ⁧لٰكِنَّ⁩ ) and vowels ( ⁧مِنَ المَحَطَّة⁩ , ⁧كَانَتِ المَدِينَة⁩ );
• the vowels of suffix pronouns ( ⁧نَفْسِهَا⁩ , ⁧عِنْدَنَا⁩ );

• tāʾ marbūṭa , which reads -a, or -at when the word is the first term of a 'iḍāfa ( ⁧كُرَة القَدَم⁩ → kurat al- qadam). It is the intermediate step towards the partially vocized texts of the module A2.3 and the timed reading of the end level (Plan 6.2: at least 50 words per minute).
7. Pronunciation

⁧كُنْتُ⁩ and ⁧كَانَ⁩ . kuntu, kunnā (with double n), but kāna, kānat: the rule of the two bases. ⁧مَا زِلْتُ⁩ . mā Ziltu: sound z, short. Don't say ""mā zāltu». faʿlāʾ. ḥamrāʾ, sawdāʾ, bayḍāʾ: ā long and final hamza. In front of a word that begins with the article the hamza is heard: ⁧سَيَّارَةٌ بَيْضَاءُ اللَّوْنِ⁩ A white car is a white car. ⁧شَعْر⁩ and ⁧شِعْر⁩ . šaʿr Hair (s) (s) / šiʿr Poetry: trains the difference between a and after š.

Reading 1 · How Milan was (without any termination)
⁧جَاءَ أَبُو لُوكَا مِن جَنُوب إِيطَالِيَا إِلَى مِيلَانُو قَبْل خَمْسِين سَنَة. كَانَ شَابّا، وَكَانَ يَعْمَل فِي مَصْنَع كَبِير⁩
⁧لِلسَّيَّارَات. كَانَ يَسْكُن مَعَ ثَلَاثَة عُمَّال فِي شَقَّة صَغِيرَة قَرِيبَة مِنَ المَحَطَّة.⁩
⁧فِي ذٰلِكَ الوَقْت كَانَتِ المَدِينَة رَمَادِيَّة، وَكَانَ الجَوّ بَارِدا فِي الشِّتَاء. كُنَّا نَعْمَل مِنَ الصَّبَاح حَتَّى⁩ » ⁧يَقُول أَبُو لُوكَا:⁩
⁧المَسَاء، وَيَوْم الأَحَد كُنَّا نَلْعَب كُرَة القَدَم فِي حَدِيقَة الحَيّ. لَمْ تَكُن هُنَاكَ مَطَاعِم أَجْنَبِيَّة، وَلَمْ يَكُن عِنْدَنَا هَاتِف⁩
« ⁧فِي البَيْت.⁩
⁧اليَوْم تَغَيَّرَ كُلّ شَيْء. أَصْبَحَ المَصْنَع مَرْكَزا تِجَارِيّا، وَصَارَ الحَيّ مُزْدَحِما بِالسَّيَّارَات وَالمَحَلَّات. فِي الحَيّ الآنَ⁩
⁧مَطَاعِم مِصْرِيَّة وَمَغْرِبِيَّة وَصِينِيَّة، وَيَسْكُن فِيهِ نَاس مِن بِلَاد كَثِيرَة.⁩
⁧لٰكِنَّ أَبَا لُوكَا لَا يَزَال يَمْشِي كُلّ صَبَاح إِلَى الحَدِيقَة نَفْسِهَا، وَمَا زَالَ يَشْتَرِي الجَرِيدَة مِنَ الكُشْك نَفْسِه. يَقُول:⁩
« ⁧المَدِينَة تَغَيَّرَتْ، وَأَنَا مَا زِلْتُ مِثْل زَمَان!⁩ »

Reading 2 · A witness
Teaching text invented.
⁧كُنْتُ أَنْتَظِرُ الحَافِلَةَ أَمَامَ البَنْكِ، وَرَأَيْتُ رَجُلَيْنِ يَخْرُجَانِ مِنْ سَيَّارَةٍ رَمَادِيَّةٍ. الأَوَّلُ كَانَ طَوِيلًا⁩ » ⁧قَالَ الشَّاهِدُ:⁩
⁧وَنَحِيفًا، شَعْرُهُ أَسْوَدُ، وَلَهُ لِحْيَةٌ قَصِيرَةٌ. كَانَ يَلْبَسُ قَمِيصًا أَبْيَضَ. الثَّانِي كَانَ قَصِيرًا وَأَصْلَعَ، وَكَانَ يَلْبَسُ⁩
⁧نَظَّارَةً سَوْدَاءَ وَقُبَّعَةً حَمْرَاءَ. دَخَلَا البَنْكَ، وَبَعْدَ خَمْسِ دَقَائِقَ خَرَجَا بِسُرْعَةٍ وَرَكِبَا السَّيَّارَةَ. لَمْ أَرَ رَقْمَ السَّيَّارَةِ،⁩
« ⁧لٰكِنِّي مَا زِلْتُ أَتَذَكَّرُ وَجْهَيْهِمَا جَيِّدًا.⁩

12. Writing
Exercise 12 · How I was ten years ago

Write about 100 words vocalized about you ten years ago and today. Compulsory elements: at least five habits with ⁧كَانَ⁩ + imperfect; two punctual actions to the perfect; two changes with ⁧أَصْبَحَ⁩ or ⁧صَارَ⁩ ; something that you keep doing with ⁧مَا زَالَ⁩ or ⁧لَا يَزَالُ⁩ ; something you don't do anymore ( ⁧لَمْ يَعُدْ⁩ ); a brief description of your appearance at the time (hair, glasses, beard...).
